model_family: Wav2Vec 2.0 base (frozen, first 6 transformer layers) + linear head
prediction: vocal emotion expressed in one audio clip
intended_use: Educational demo of speech emotion recognition. Shows the emotion a short clip's voice most resembles, with the model's uncertainty.
not_for: any statement about a person's mental health or wellbeing

metrics.evaluation: leave-one-speaker-out over 14 speakers (acted speech); layer chosen inside each fold
metrics.cpu_latency_note: median of 15 runs, 4 threads, measured side by side with the SVM (314 ms) and the full 12-layer backbone (919 ms) in one session; absolute times varied about 2x between sessions on this machine

limitations: Trained only on acted speech (Emo-DB: 10 German actors; SAVEE: 4 male English actors). Natural, everyday speech is usually much less exaggerated.
Only 14 speakers in total, so results vary a lot from one speaker to another.
Recording conditions (studio microphones) differ from phones and laptops; background noise lowers accuracy.
It estimates the emotion expressed in the voice in one clip. It does not measure how a person feels overall, their mood over time, or their mental health.
Only six emotion categories are recognised; everything else is forced into one of them.
Evaluation scores come from held-out actors in the same two corpora, not from real-world use.
The backbone was pretrained on English read speech (LibriSpeech); it was not trained for emotion.
Trained on one corpus and tested on the other, every model scored poorly (best macro-F1 about 0.25), so expect much lower accuracy on everyday recordings than on the acted test speakers.
